title: A negative lower co-Choi direction becomes an upper-domination failure after tensor squaring

statement.quantifiers: For Phi=(Tr(.)I2-id/2)^tensor2 on two physical qubits, u=(1,0,0,1), and M_u(E_ab)=Phi(e_a u*)Phi(uu*)^-1 Phi(u e_b*).
statement.assertion: The explicit v satisfies v*Rv=9 and v*Sv=-11, so R+S is not PSD. On four physical qubits with reference u tensor u, v tensor v gives (R tensor R-S tensor S) expectation -40, normalized -5/98.
assumptions: Input-first co-Choi convention and canonical regrouping of tensor factors.
A=I4+uu*/4 and A^-1=I4-uu*/6; reference rescaling leaves M_u unchanged.

inputs: Exact finite R,S built from the specified reduction map/reference, not exploratory saved floating arrays.
outputs: Exact disproof of arbitrary-entangled-reference sufficient co-Choi domination.

proof_mechanism: Compute A and inverse exactly, construct ell_a, then R=Jhat(Phi),S=Jhat(M_u).
Check Sv=-11Rv/9, yielding expectations9,-11 and lower-domination violation-2.

obstructions: Local qubit reduction map is CP, so its tensor powers satisfy actual positivity; the sufficient certificate is stronger than the target property.
This is not Werner distillability, a qutrit counterexample, NPT bound entanglement, or a refutation of the valid product-reference subclass.
